assets.alt: The same Africa coastline appears upright on the left and rotated a quarter turn on the right. Each orientation has a matching direction marker.
assets.prompt: Authored text-free SVG diagram: The same Africa coastline appears upright on the left and rotated a quarter turn on the right. Each orientation has a matching direction marker.
assets.title: A map can turn
assets.caption: The map on the right turns so east is at the top. Its direction marker turns with it. North at the top is a useful convention, not a physical rule.

assets.alt: Left: Mercator coastlines make Greenland appear close to Africa in area. Right: equal-area coastlines at one scale show Africa much larger than Greenland.
assets.prompt: Authored text-free SVG diagram: Left: Mercator coastlines make Greenland appear close to Africa in area. Right: equal-area coastlines at one scale show Africa much larger than Greenland.
assets.title: Flattening changes size
assets.caption: Mercator stretches areas far from the equator. In the right panel both shapes use equal-area projections at one common scale: Africa has about fourteen times Greenland’s land area. Coastlines come from Natural Earth.

assets.title: A round surface laid flat
assets.caption: The curved segments stand for strips of a round surface. Gaps appear when they lie flat. Closing the gaps requires stretching or changing the representation.
